title: Population Genetics of Prompts: Drift and Selection in Self-Refinement Loops

original_idea.body:
# Population Genetics of Prompts: Drift and Selection in Self-Refinement Loops

**Problem:** Iterated self-improvement / self-refinement loops are a theoretical concern (value drift over recursion), but we lack quantitative models of how content evolves under repeated model-mediated mutation and selection.

**Direction:** Borrow drift-vs-selection models from population genetics. Run an open model through many rounds of paraphrase/refine ('mutation') with a fixed scoring filter ('selection'), tracking a measurable trait (sentiment, hedging, factual accuracy, a target value-statement) across generations. Fit a simple selection-coefficient/drift model and measure whether traits fixate, drift, or collapse — characterizing alignment-relevant attractor states.

**Why it matters:** Imports a rigorous evolutionary framework to study recursive-self-modification value drift, a quintessential long-horizon risk labs cannot prioritize. Fully training-free, runs locally, and yields interpretable quantitative dynamics.

**Relevant context:** Drift/selection dynamics are foundational in population genetics. Vingean reflection and recursive self-improvement are formal_theoretical open problems (Alignment Forum). Self-refinement loops are easily simulated with open models.
